equation_request.abstract:
We consider the Unitary Permutation problem which consists, given $n$ unitary gates $U_{1},\ldots,U_{n}$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, in applying the unitary gates in the order specified by $\sigma$, i.e. in performing $U_{\sigma(n)}\circ\ldots\circ U_{\sigma(1)}$.

This problem has been introduced and investigated in [7] where two models of computations are considered. This first is the (standard) model of query complexity: the complexity measure is the number of calls to any of the unitary gates $U_{i}$ in a quantum circuit which solves the problem. The second model provides quantum switches and treats unitary transformations as inputs of second order. In that case the complexity measure is the number of quantum switches. In their paper, Colnaghi et al. [7] have shown that the problem can be solved within $n^{2}$ calls in the query model and $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ quantum switches in the new model.

We refine these results by proving that $n\log_{2}(n)+\Theta(n)$ quantum switches are necessary and sufficient to solve this problem, whereas $n^{2}-2n+4$ calls are sufficient to solve this problem in the standard quantum circuit model. We prove, with an additional assumption on the family of gates used in the circuits, that $n^{2}-o(n^{7/4+\epsilon})$ queries are required, for any $\epsilon>0$. The upper and lower bounds for the standard quantum circuit model are established by pointing out connections with the permutation as substring problem introduced by Karp.

specification.problem: Unitary Permutation problem: given n black-box unitary gates U_1,...,U_n (same dimension) and a permutation sigma of {1,...,n}, implement the composite U_{sigma(n)} o ... o U_{sigma(1)}. The abstract reports (i) in the standard query model a fixed circuit using n^2-2n+4 calls to the U_i suffices, with a lower bound n^2-o(n^{7/4+eps}) under an extra assumption on the gate family, via connections with Karp's 'permutation as substring/subsequence' problem; (ii) in the quantum-switch model n log2(n)+Theta(n) switches are necessary and sufficient.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to the query-model upper bound only: a fixed (sigma-independent) circuit that reads a quantum control register |sigma> and applies U_sigma to a data register using exactly L=|w| black-box calls, where w is a word over {1,...,n} containing every permutation as a subsequence (Karp's problem). Smallest useful instance chosen: n=3, single-qubit gates, w=1213121 of length 7=3^2-2*3+4. Outside scope: the quantum-switch construction achieving n log2(n)+Theta(n) switches and its matching lower bound; the query lower bound n^2-o(n^{7/4+eps}) and the 'additional assumption on the family of gates'; general-n constructions of optimal Karp words. These are the paper's main contributions beyond the upper bound and are not reconstructed here.

symbols.meaning: i-th black-box unitary gate, accessible only by calls
permutation specifying the application order; sigma(k) is the index of the k-th gate applied
fixed word (query schedule) over the gate alphabet; the j-th call is to U_{w_j}
length of w = number of black-box calls
symbols.domain: positive integer; L = n^2-2n+4 claimed sufficient; instance L=7

symbols.meaning: position in w where the k-th gate of sigma is embedded (chosen embedding of sigma as a subsequence of w)
activity bit: 1 if call j acts on the data register for permutation sigma, 0 if it is diverted to a dummy register
multiplicity of symbol i in w

symbols.domain: n*ceil(log2 n) qubits; block k (k=1 leftmost) holds binary of sigma(k)-1
d-dimensional; one qubit in the instance

symbols.meaning: dummy register reserved for diverted calls to U_i
symbols.domain: d-dimensional; one qubit each in the instance; needed only if m_i >= 2

symbols.meaning: final sigma-independent state of the dummy registers

equations.label: Target composite unitary
equations.latex: U_{\sigma} := U_{\sigma(n)} \circ \cdots \circ U_{\sigma(1)} = U_{\sigma(n)} U_{\sigma(n-1)} \cdots U_{\sigma(1)}
equations.description: The unitary that must be implemented: U_{sigma(1)} is applied first, U_{sigma(n)} last.
equations.justification: Directly stated as the definition of the Unitary Permutation problem.
assumptions: All U_i act on the same d-dimensional system.

equations.label: Fixed circuit controlled by a quantum permutation register
equations.latex: W\big(|\sigma\rangle_{C} \otimes |\psi\rangle_{D} \otimes |0\rangle_{A_1\cdots A_n t}\big) = |\sigma\rangle_{C} \otimes \big(U_{\sigma}|\psi\rangle\big)_{D} \otimes |g\rangle_{A_1\cdots A_n} \otimes |0\rangle_{t}, \quad \forall\, \sigma \in S_n,\ \forall\, |\psi\rangle,\ \text{with } |g\rangle \text{ independent of } \sigma,\psi
equations.description: Correctness condition for a single sigma-independent circuit W that contains L black-box calls; by linearity it also works on superpositions of permutations because the residual ancilla state is sigma-independent.
equations.abstract_quote: the complexity measure is the number of calls to any of the unitary gates $U_{i}$ in a quantum circuit which solves the problem
equations.justification: If sigma were a fixed classical parameter, n calls would trivially suffice, so nontrivial bounds of order n^2 only make sense for a single circuit that must work for every sigma supplied as input (as in the second-order/quantum-switch setting of [7]). The sigma-independence of |g> is my requirement to make the circuit valid on superpositions.
assumptions: sigma is supplied as a computational-basis state of register C (possibly in superposition).
Ancilla registers may be left in a fixed sigma-independent state.

equations.label: Karp permutation-supersequence word (query schedule)
equations.latex: w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_L \in \{1,\ldots,n\}^{L},\quad L = n^{2}-2n+4,\quad \forall \sigma \in S_n\ \exists\, p_\sigma(1) < p_\sigma(2) < \cdots < p_\sigma(n):\ w_{p_\sigma(k)} = \sigma(k)\ (k=1,\ldots,n)
equations.description: A word over the gate alphabet containing every permutation of {1,...,n} as a (not necessarily contiguous) subsequence; its length equals the number of calls of the circuit.
equations.abstract_quote: $n^{2}-2n+4$ calls are sufficient to solve this problem in the standard quantum circuit model. We prove, with an additional assumption on the family of gates used in the circuits, that $n^{2}-o(n^{7/4+\epsilon})$ queries are required, for any $\epsilon>0$. The upper and lower bounds for the standard quantum circuit model are established by pointing out connections with the permutation as substring problem introduced by Karp.
equations.justification: The abstract ties both query bounds to Karp's problem; the stated numbers n^2-2n+4 and n^2-o(n^{7/4+eps}) coincide (to my recollection) with the known upper bound (Adleman; Galbiati–Preparata) and the Kleitman–Kwiatkowski lower bound on the shortest sequence containing all permutations as subsequences. I therefore infer that the circuit calls the gates in the order given by such a word. The existence of such a word for every n is recalled background, not verified here.
assumptions: Existence of a word of length n^2-2n+4 with the all-permutations-subsequence property (recalled from the literature for n >= 3; for n=3 verified by the explicit instance eq_7).

equations.label: Activity bits and per-call routing operator
equations.description: The j-th call to U_{w_j} acts on the data register if position j belongs to the chosen embedding of sigma, otherwise on the dummy register reserved for gate w_j. Identity on all unmentioned registers.
equations.justification: My proposed realisation of the 'subsequence -> circuit' connection: exactly n of the L calls are routed to the data register, in the order sigma(1),...,sigma(n). Any deterministic rule for choosing p_sigma (e.g. greedy leftmost embedding) may be used.
assumptions: A fixed deterministic embedding p_sigma is chosen classically for each sigma.
Controlled operations conditioned on C are allowed and do not count as queries.

equations.label: Implementation of G_j with one black-box call
equations.description: T_j is a reversible classical computation of the activity bit into ancilla t; CSWAP^{(t=0)} swaps D and A_{w_j} when t=0 (identity when t=1). The single black-box call U_{w_j} is always applied to wire D; routing is done by the swaps, so no controlled-U_i is required. t is uncomputed afterwards.
equations.justification: Black-box calls cannot be controlled directly in the query model, so routing of the data by controlled swaps is the standard way to make a call act conditionally; this uses exactly one query per j.
assumptions: Controlled-SWAP and the classical reversible circuit T_j are free (not counted as queries).

equations.label: Full circuit, residual ancilla state and query count
equations.latex: W = G_L \cdots G_2 G_1, \qquad |g\rangle = \bigotimes_{i=1}^{n} \big(U_i^{\,m_i-1}|0\rangle\big)_{A_i},\quad m_i = |\{j : w_j = i\}|, \qquad \#\text{calls} = L = n^{2}-2n+4
equations.description: Composing the G_j realises eq_2: the n active calls apply U_{sigma(1)},...,U_{sigma(n)} to D in order; each gate i is diverted exactly m_i-1 times to its own dummy A_i, so the dummy state does not depend on sigma. Exact equality, no approximation.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_3–eq_5 by direct composition: for each sigma the data register sees exactly the subsequence w_{p_sigma(1)},...,w_{p_sigma(n)} = sigma(1),...,sigma(n); every symbol i occurs once actively, hence m_i-1 times passively, independent of sigma. The query count equals |w|, matching the abstract's upper bound.
assumptions: Dummy registers are initialised to |0> (any fixed state works).

equations.label: Explicit tiny instance n=3
equations.description: The word 1213121 contains all six permutations of {1,2,3} as subsequences (123:1,2,4; 132:1,4,6; 213:2,3,4; 231:2,4,5; 312:4,5,6; 321:4,6,7). Registers: C = 6 qubits (three 2-qubit blocks holding sigma(k)-1), D = 1 qubit, A_1 and A_2 = 1 qubit each (A_3 unnecessary since m_3=1), t = 1 qubit.
equations.justification: Smallest n for which the abstract's formula n^2-2n+4 equals the (recalled) optimal Karp length; chosen as the concrete instance in the absence of an experiment scope. Subsequence check done by hand above.
assumptions: Single-qubit gates U_1,U_2,U_3 as black boxes.

equations.label: Quantum switch (second-order primitive, background only)
equations.latex: S(U,V)\,\big(|c\rangle \otimes |\psi\rangle\big) = \begin{cases} |0\rangle \otimes V U |\psi\rangle & c=0 \\ |1\rangle \otimes U V |\psi\rangle & c=1 \end{cases}
equations.description: A quantum switch takes two unitaries as inputs and applies them in one of two orders controlled coherently by a qubit; the switch-model complexity counts such primitives. Only the definition is recalled; the n log2(n)+Theta(n) construction is not reconstructed.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the quantum switch as used in Colnaghi et al. and the indefinite-causal-order literature; included to make the scope boundary explicit.
assumptions: Convention for which order corresponds to c=0 is arbitrary.

registers.name: C
registers.role: holds the permutation |sigma>; block k (k=1 leftmost) stores sigma(k)-1 in binary; unchanged by the circuit

registers.name: D
registers.size: log2 d qubits (1 for the instance)
registers.role: data register on which U_sigma is applied

registers.name: A_i (i=1..n)
registers.size: log2 d qubits each (1 each; A_i omitted if m_i = 1)
registers.role: dummy register absorbing the m_i-1 inactive calls to U_i; ends in the sigma-independent state U_i^{m_i-1}|0>

registers.name: t
registers.role: ancilla holding the activity bit a_j(sigma) during call j; returned to |0>

specification.initial_state: |sigma>_C (or any superposition of permutation basis states) ⊗ |psi>_D ⊗ |0...0>_{A_1...A_n} ⊗ |0>_t, with register order C ⊗ D ⊗ A_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ A_n ⊗ t.

steps.description: Fix the query schedule: choose a word w over {1,...,n} of length L containing every permutation as a subsequence (instance: w=1213121), and for each sigma fix an embedding p_sigma and the activity bits a_j(sigma).
For j = 1,...,L: compute a_j(sigma) into t (T_j); if t=0 swap D with A_{w_j}; call U_{w_j} on wire D (one query); if t=0 swap back; uncompute t (T_j^dagger).
After all L calls the data register holds U_sigma|psi>, C is unchanged, and the dummy registers hold the sigma-independent state |g>; total queries L = n^2-2n+4 (7 for n=3).

assumptions: The permutation sigma is provided as a quantum register input (as in the second-order setting of Colnaghi et al.), so a single sigma-independent circuit is required; otherwise the problem is trivial with n calls.
Black boxes U_i can only be invoked as plain calls on a chosen wire (no controlled-U_i); routing via controlled-SWAP and classical reversible logic conditioned on C is free.
All gates act on the same d-dimensional system; the instance uses d=2 (single-qubit gates) and n=3.
Existence of a word of length n^2-2n+4 containing all permutations of {1,...,n} as subsequences is recalled from the literature on Karp's problem and only verified here for n=3.
The per-gate dummy-register construction (eq_4–eq_6) is my proposed realisation of the abstract's Karp connection, not a verified reproduction of the paper's circuit.
Equation eq_8 is background only; the switch-model results are not reconstructed.
missing_information: The paper's explicit quantum-switch circuit achieving n log2(n)+Theta(n) switches and the proof of the matching lower bound.
The 'additional assumption on the family of gates' under which the n^2-o(n^{7/4+eps}) query lower bound holds, and the reduction to Karp's problem used in the proof.
Whether the paper's query model treats sigma as a classical description or a quantum control register, and what output is required on ancillas.
The specific Karp word of length n^2-2n+4 used for general n and the paper's own routing/ancilla scheme.
The dimension d of the gates and any restrictions on the gate family.
